newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Thursday thanks to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,350 yuan ($2,450) per tonne, rising 50 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,550 and hit a low of 20,320.
October fell 70 to 20,700 yuan and November 40 to 20,480. December ended unchanged at 20,350. February and March rose 20 to 20,350 and April 300 to 20,400.
Combined volume fell to 32,180 tonnes from 41,310.
Copper opened up on gains on the LME but did not hold above the key 20,500-yuan resistance level, which triggered selling that pushed contracts to their intra-day lows, traders said.
"Hedge-selling and speculative selling triggered panic selling late in the session because copper did not breach the 20,500-yuan level this morning," one trader said.
"Many investors believed that copper would not rise sharply in the absence of big market-moving news," he added.
Traders said that copper on the LME had consolidated in a narrow range for a long time, which made many Shanghai investors stay on the sidelines.
"Many investors lost interest in trading and the open interest of most contracts decreased on uncertainties in the market," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to continue moving in a narrow range of 20,000 and 20,500 in the short term.
Aluminium ended little changed. October rose 70 to 14,000. November and December closed unchanged at 14,000.
Combined volume fell to 370 tonnes from 500.
